gaps.title: Delete: confirmation, recoverability and effect on existing shares
gaps.description: The Documents table shows an enabled delete (trash icon) button, but no confirmation state or post-delete state is shown in the capture. It is not stated whether deletion is permanent or recoverable, for how long, or what happens to colleagues who currently have viewer or editor access to the deleted document.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003: 'Delete: is there a confirmation step, and is deletion permanent or recoverable?'
ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003: 'Delete: what happens to existing shares of a deleted document?'

gaps.why_it_matters: DEC-001 confirms delete as part of managing documents for every signed-in employee, and DEC-005 lets owners share documents with colleagues, so one owner's deletion can remove a document other colleagues rely on. The trash icon sits in the same row as Share, so accidental activation is plausible.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Documents may be lost irrecoverably by a mis-click, and colleagues with shared access may lose work without warning; recovery requests cannot be handled consistently.
research_questions: How do Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive handle deletion of a shared document: trash retention period, restore, and what collaborators see?
What do established UX guidelines (for example Nielsen Norman Group) recommend between confirmation dialogs and undo for deleting a single file?

gaps.title: Share flow is not captured: choosing colleagues, setting viewer/editor, revoking
gaps.description: DEC-005 defines sharing (named colleagues, viewer or editor, revoke at any time, no public links), but the capture shows only a Share button; no share dialog, colleague selection, permission choice, list of current collaborators, revoke control, or success/failure feedback is shown in the capture. No flows were recorded.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003: 'Share: can sharing be revoked, and what feedback is shown?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Sharing is the only control over who can open a document (DEC-004), so the share and revoke steps are where the security requirement is enforced. How a colleague is identified and how current access is displayed determine whether owners can see and correct who has access.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The sharing workflow and revoke workflow cannot be specified or tested; owners may grant access to the wrong colleague or be unable to confirm that access was removed.
research_questions: In Google Drive's share dialog, how are named people selected, how are viewer/editor roles shown and changed, and how is access removed?
What feedback do comparable tools give the owner and the recipient after sharing and after revoking access?

gaps.title: Rights of viewers and editors, and where shared documents appear
gaps.description: DEC-001 limits managing to an employee's own documents, and DEC-005 introduces viewer and editor roles, but it is not stated what an editor may do (edit content, rename, upload new versions, delete, re-share) or what a viewer may do (open, download). It is also not stated whether documents shared with a user appear in the Documents table shown, which displays only one row and no owner column.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003: 'Delete: who can delete a document?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The Share and Delete buttons are shown enabled on the row; without defined role rights it is unclear whether a non-owner would see or be able to use them, which directly affects the security requirement that only people the owner shares with can open a document.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Editors could delete or re-share documents beyond the owner's intent, or recipients may have no way to find documents shared with them.
research_questions: What exactly can a Google Drive 'Editor' versus 'Viewer' do on a file (rename, delete, re-share, download), and which of these can the owner restrict?

gaps.title: Rename is confirmed but not supported by any captured control
gaps.description: DEC-001 includes rename in managing documents, but no rename control, inline edit or rename dialog is shown in the capture. Rules for name validation (allowed characters, length, duplicate names, file extension) are not stated.

evidence_refs.locator: DEC-001 verbatim 'upload, rename, delete and share'

gaps.why_it_matters: Rename is one of the four confirmed management actions and must meet the two-click criterion, yet there is no observed entry point to measure against.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Rename cannot be specified or tested; name collisions or invalid names may corrupt how documents are listed and shared.
research_questions: How do comparable document tools (Google Drive, OneDrive) handle renaming to a name that already exists in the same library, and changes to the file extension?

gaps.title: Upload rules and outcomes are not defined
gaps.description: The Upload button is shown, but allowed file types, maximum file size, multiple-file upload, behaviour when a same-named document exists, progress feedback, failure handling and repeated submissions are not stated, and no upload state is shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Upload is the way documents enter the library, which DEC-003 sizes at up to 1,000 documents; file limits and duplicate-name behaviour shape storage, the two-second page target and whether existing documents can be silently replaced.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Uploads may fail without explanation, overwrite existing documents, or create duplicates from double clicks.
research_questions: What upload progress, failure and duplicate-name conventions do Google Drive and OneDrive use for single and multiple file uploads?

gaps.title: Behaviour of the document list at up to 1,000 documents
gaps.description: REQ-005 requires pages to load within two seconds for up to 1,000 documents, but the capture shows a single row. Sort order, pagination or scrolling, search and filtering, and how the 'Modified' value is shown for older documents are not stated or shown.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003: 'How is the list sorted, paginated or searched, and what is shown when it is empty?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The two-second target is stated for a 1,000-document library, so how many rows a page shows and how users find a document determine both whether the target is testable and whether managing documents remains 'easy' at that size.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The performance requirement cannot be verified against a defined page, and users with large libraries may be unable to find documents within the two-click criterion.
research_questions: What default sort, page size and search patterns do file-management tools use for lists in the range of 1,000 items?
How is page load time commonly measured for acceptance (for example Core Web Vitals LCP thresholds)?

gaps.title: Empty, loading, success and error states not shown in the capture
gaps.description: Only the default state of the Documents screen was captured. The empty library, loading, and the success and failure states for upload, rename, share, revoke and delete are not shown in the capture.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003: 'What happens on failure of Share or Delete?'

gaps.why_it_matters: New employees will start with an empty library, and every one of the four confirmed actions changes data or access; without defined outcomes users cannot tell whether a share, revoke or delete took effect.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users may repeat actions or believe access was revoked when it was not; the states cannot be designed or tested.
research_questions: How should status messages for upload, share and delete results be announced to meet WCAG 2.2 success criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages)?

gaps.title: How the 'at most two clicks' criterion is measured
gaps.description: DEC-001 defines 'easily' as each action taking at most two clicks, but it is not stated where counting starts, whether choosing a file, selecting a colleague, choosing viewer or editor, or confirming a delete count as clicks, or whether keyboard use is covered.

evidence_refs.locator: DEC-001 verbatim 'each takes at most two clicks'

gaps.why_it_matters: Sharing requires naming a colleague and a role (DEC-005), and delete may need a confirmation (GAP-001); depending on how clicks are counted these steps may or may not fit the confirmed criterion.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The usability criterion cannot be tested, and it may be in tension with safety steps for delete and sharing.

gaps.title: Icon-only delete button and unlabeled actions column
gaps.description: The delete control is shown as a trash icon only, and the table's actions column has no visible header. Whether these controls have accessible names identifying the document they act on, and how they behave with keyboard and screen readers, is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: With up to 1,000 rows each carrying Share and Delete, assistive-technology users must be able to tell which document a destructive action applies to; the feature is for every signed-in employee.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Screen-reader users may delete or share the wrong document, and the screen may fail WCAG 2.2 AA.
research_questions: Which WCAG 2.2 AA success criteria (for example 1.1.1, 2.4.6, 4.1.2) apply to icon-only row action buttons in data tables, and what do they require of their accessible names?

gaps.title: Whether colleagues are notified when access is granted or revoked
gaps.description: It is not stated whether a colleague is told that a document was shared with them or that their access was revoked, through which channel, or what happens if that notice fails.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003: 'Share: can sharing be revoked, and what feedback is shown?'

gaps.why_it_matters: DEC-005 says sharing should work like Google Drive with named colleagues; whether recipients learn of new or removed access affects how shared documents are discovered (GAP-003).
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Recipients may not know a document is available to them, or may be surprised by lost access.
research_questions: What does Google Drive notify recipients of when a file is shared with them or when their access is removed, and can the sharer suppress the notice?

gaps.title: Documents and shares of employees who leave or lose access
gaps.description: Ownership is tied to each employee's own documents, but it is not stated what happens to an employee's documents and the access granted on them when the account is deactivated or deleted, or whether ownership can be transferred.

evidence_refs.locator: DEC-001 verbatim 'every signed-in employee on their own documents'
DEC-004 verbatim 'only people the owner shares a document with can open it'

gaps.why_it_matters: Because only the owner can grant access (DEC-004, DEC-005), a departed owner leaves shared documents with no one able to manage access or delete them.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Shared documents may become orphaned, inaccessible to the team, or retained indefinitely.

gaps.title: Revoked access or deletion while a colleague has the document open
gaps.description: It is not stated what a colleague sees if their access is revoked, their role changes, or the document is deleted while they have it open or are editing it, nor how simultaneous edits by an owner and an editor are handled.

evidence_refs.locator: DEC-005 verbatim 'can revoke access at any time'

gaps.why_it_matters: DEC-005 allows revoking at any time and grants an editor role, so mid-session changes in access are expected; DEC-004 requires that only people with current access can open the document.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: A revoked colleague may keep access in an open session, or an editor may lose unsaved changes without explanation.
research_questions: How do Google Drive and OneDrive handle a user whose access is removed while the file is open in their session?

assumptions.text: The employee who uploads a document is its owner.
assumptions.why: DEC-001 and DEC-004 refer to 'own documents' and 'the owner' without defining ownership.
assumptions.impact: Determines who may share, revoke, rename and delete each document.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm that the uploader is the owner and whether ownership can change.

assumptions.text: The Documents table on SCR-001 lists the signed-in employee's own documents.
assumptions.why: The capture shows one row with no owner column and no indication of shared items.
assumptions.impact: Affects whether a separate view or indicator is needed for documents shared with the user.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm which documents the table is meant to list.

proposed_status_changes.reason: The rights of the viewer and editor roles (rename, delete, re-share, download) are not defined (GAP-003).
Whether delete is permanent or recoverable, and its effect on existing shares, is not defined (GAP-001).
